title: Remulla warns of ‘micro hubs’ in Metro Manila as scam operations evolve
summary: MANILA, Philippines — Authorities are tracking three active micro scam hubs in Metro Manila that are allegedly linked to dismissed police and military officers, Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla said…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Authorities are tracking three active micro scam hubs in Metro Manila that are allegedly linked to dismissed police and military officers, Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla said on Wednesday. Remulla cited the Oct. 2 raid on a suspected scam hub in Zamboanga Sibugay, which authorities described as the largest raid on a Philippine offshore gaming operator (Pogo) since the nationwide ban on the industry two years ago. The operation led to the arrest and rescue of 244 foreign nationals, mostly Chinese. “We caught the one in Zamboanga Sibugay. We’re actively tracking three more here in the Metro Manila area,” Remulla said at a press conference during the 20th Asean Ministerial Meeting on Transnational Crime in Makati City. READ: 200 foreign nationals found in suspected scam hub in Sibugay Remulla said the operations use “micro hubs,” or small houses where 10 to 20 people stay in each location. He described the setup as a new trend in scamming operations. “It’s not like before. Before, what we had here had 5,000 people in one building. Now they rent small houses.
